questions.q: Describe the main types of farming.
answer: Agriculture is a primary activity, and it is practised in several ways depending on land, labour and purpose.

answer.text: Here crops are grown mainly to feed the farmer's own family. It may be intensive, using small plots and much labour, or primitive shifting cultivation, in which a patch of forest is cleared and burnt, cultivated for a few years and then abandoned — known as jhum in north-east India.
Crops and livestock are raised on a large scale for sale in the market, using machinery, fertilisers and high-yielding seeds.
A single cash crop, such as tea, coffee, rubber or sugarcane, is grown on large estates, mostly for export.

questions.q: Describe the cropping seasons of India and the conditions needed for rice and wheat.

answer.text: India has three main cropping seasons. Kharif crops, such as rice, maize and cotton, are sown with the arrival of the monsoon in June and July and harvested in September and October. Rabi crops, such as wheat, gram and mustard, are sown in winter and harvested in spring. Zaid crops, such as watermelon, are grown in the short summer season.

Rice needs high temperature, high humidity and plentiful rainfall, and grows well in the river plains and coastal areas. Wheat needs moderate temperature and rainfall during its growing season and bright sunshine at harvest, and is grown mainly in the northern plains.
